In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

UMLDiff is a promising tool that can help developers to better manage the complexity of object-oriented design change and to better understand the rationale behind the design evolution of object-oriented software systems.

UMLDiff is a robust and accurate algorithm for automatically detecting the structural differences between two object-oriented designs, and that the analyses it enables are useful for understanding the evolution of object-oriented designs and planning future design evolution.
UMLDiff provides a good solution to the problem of automatically detecting structural design changes in object-oriented software.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

UMLDiff is a robust, accurate, and effective algorithm for automatically detecting design changes in object-oriented systems, and it enables a number of design-evolution analyses that can support a number of design evolution tasks.

UMLDiff is a robust and effective tool for reverse engineering and analyzing design evolution of object-oriented software, which has been successfully applied to a number of industrial projects and has been used as a basis of several other reverse engineering and design evolution analysis tools.

UMLDiff is the first tool for automatically detecting design evolution at the level of packages, classes and methods, and that it provides an important step towards the goal of supporting software evolution activities.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the proposed algorithm can be used to automatically detect structural changes between the design versions of a software system, and that these changes can be used to support various software-evolution activities.

, by reverse engineering two versions of a software system and applying UMLDiff to detect design evolution, one can produce a design evolution report that is more accurate, complete, and fine-grained than those produced by the existing design evolution tools.
